nodes.label: Pattern 11: NumPy for numerical operations
nodes.rationale: Use only for large numeric workloads where NumPy is an approved dependency; include array allocation and conversion costs in the benchmark.

nodes.label: Pattern 12: Caching with functools.lru_cache
nodes.rationale: Use only when arguments are hashable and cached values remain valid for the cache lifetime; bound caches when inputs can grow without limit.

nodes.label: Pattern 13: __slots__ for memory
nodes.rationale: Measure object counts and total memory before adopting this tradeoff; __slots__ changes instance behavior.

nodes.label: Pattern 14: Multiprocessing for CPU-bound tasks
nodes.rationale: Use only after measuring CPU saturation and accounting for process startup, serialization, platform behavior, and shutdown.

nodes.label: Pattern 15: Async I/O for I/O-bound tasks
nodes.norm_label: pattern 15: async i/o for i/o-bound tasks
nodes.rationale: Use only when surrounding application is async and HTTP/client dependencies are approved; keep external endpoints out of local-first production paths.

nodes.label: Pattern 16: Batch database operations
nodes.rationale: Keep transactions bounded and preserve rollback/error behavior.

nodes.label: Pattern 17: Query optimization
nodes.rationale: Inspect query plans and add indexes only for measured access patterns; verify write and storage costs.

nodes.label: Pattern 19: Iterators vs lists
nodes.rationale: Iterator uses constant memory; list loads entire file into memory.

nodes.label: Pattern 20: Weak references for caches
nodes.rationale: Weak references do not retain values; callers need another strong reference while using a cached resource.

nodes.label: Performance testing with pytest-benchmark
nodes.rationale: Use only when the project already provides this dependency; otherwise use its existing test and benchmark tooling.
